text:
Seth Jones has 23 points in 23 games, and 15 of them came on the power play. That is the shape of his season in Florida: a 32-year-old with more than 900 NHL games behind him (24.5 minutes a night here) who has become the man the Panthers' power play runs through. He has scored at 2.45 points per 60 minutes, well above the 1.47 to 2.11 range our numbers think is his true level, so some of this pace is the hot hand.

Not all of it, though. His own scoring is a touch unlucky: three goals on 3.64 expected goals (expected goals measure the quality of his chances), and his teammates have scored 2.3 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. The last ten games brought eight points, roughly what we'd expect.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season shows the two sides of him. He stops 18% of the entries aimed at his blue line, against a typical 11%, but only 30% of his exits keep possession. Watch for clears off the glass when a forecheck leans on him.
headline: Seth Jones is running Florida's power play
